blocks.text: Writing the raw memory representation of a structure is not a portable file format. Padding, member layout, integer width, byte order, floating representation, compiler choices, and future version changes can all affect the bytes. Trivially copyable does not mean suitable for persistent interchange without a defined encoding.

blocks.text: Define a binary format in terms of explicit fields and byte order. For example, a four-octet unsigned quantity in network-style big-endian order places its most significant octet first. Encode it using shifts and masks in an appropriate unsigned type, and decode by combining unsigned values. State the eight-bit-byte requirement when the format is defined in octets. Do not imply that every possible C++ implementation uses that representation.
